# 2020, three audiences

## Government

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- $R_t$, the reproduction number over time. How many people each case
  goes on to infect
- We sent weekly $R_t$ estimates, forecasts and ad hoc reports to
  SPI-M-O, the UK government's modelling advisory group
- SPI-M-O reported to SAGE, the scientific advisory group for
  emergencies. The public saw a consensus statement

> We don't know whether any of this gave any policy maker any useful
> information that helped them make better decisions...
>
> *Abbott and Funk, 2022*
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-shot-spimo-statement.png){width="74%"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="GOV.UK page: SPI-M-O consensus statement, 17 September 2020"}

::: {.attribution}
[SPI-M-O consensus statement, 17 September 2020](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/spi-m-o-consensus-statement-on-covid-19-17-september-2020),
GOV.UK ·
[Reflections on two years estimating effective reproduction numbers](https://samabbott.co.uk/posts/2022-03-25-rt-reflections/),
2022
:::
:::
::::

## What the consensus process did

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Each group used its own data sources and its own model
- Evidence from several models was considered, discussed and combined
- What went out was a range. The detail behind each estimate did not

> If results are presented individually this can get lost and it
> incentivises being first out (and maybe therefore cutting corners).
>
> *Abbott, 2023*
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-uk-rt-dashboard.png){height="700px"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="GOV.UK: latest R range for England, 1.0 to 1.2, no point estimate"}

::: {.attribution}
[The R value and growth rate](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-r-value-and-growth-rate),
GOV.UK ·
[Data, Models, and Modellers during a Global Pandemic](https://samabbott.co.uk/posts/2023-01-04-iisa-data-models-and-modellers-during-a-global-pandemic/),
2023
:::
:::
::::

## The public. A map, then a page for each place

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- [epiforecasts.io/covid](https://epiforecasts.io/covid/), April 2020 to
  March 2022. Daily $R_t$ and nowcasts for several thousand locations
- A nowcast is an estimate of what has already happened but has not yet
  been reported
- The front page was a map. Five words, increasing to decreasing, and no
  numbers
- A page for each country, then for the regions inside it. Just over
  500,000 unique users and 1.2 million page views by March 2022
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-shot-covid-map.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The global page of the dashboard. A world map with countries
coloured increasing, likely increasing, stable, likely decreasing or
decreasing, with the data date and download links above it"}

::: {.attribution}
[epiforecasts.io/covid, global summary](https://epiforecasts.io/covid/posts/global/),
estimates frozen 30 March 2022, screenshot 12 September 2026 · counts
from
[Reflections on two years estimating effective reproduction numbers](https://samabbott.co.uk/posts/2022-03-25-rt-reflections/),
2022
:::
:::
::::

## The caveats sat in the captions

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Estimates from partial data were drawn in orange, adjusted for right
  truncation
- Each figure caption carried the same sentence
- The limitations sat on a methods page that 20,000 of 1.2 million page
  views reached
- The limits travel less well than the method

> These should be considered indicative only.
>
> *The figure captions, epiforecasts.io/covid*
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-shot-covid-uk-panels.png){height="760px"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="UK page of the dashboard. Cases by report date, cases by
infection date and the reproduction number, with the most recent days in

## Other governments used it too

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- The estimates went out as CSV files on GitHub. Other governments used
  them directly, or through scientists who set them beside other
  evidence
- Checking several thousand locations a day was beyond us
- Could AI do that checking?

> Of course this can cause issues if the limitations of the method are
> poorly communicated.
>
> *Abbott and Funk, 2022*
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-shot-covid-table.png){width="100%"

## What went wrong

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
> Because we did not have the capacity to manually inspect the data and
> estimates on a daily basis we sometimes published nonsensical estimates.
>
> *Abbott and Funk, 2022*

- Wisconsin reported on a Sunday for the first time. The model read the
  catch-up as an outbreak
- What I wrote down afterwards. Be as open as possible. State the
  limitations first. No point estimates
- I left the press to people whose speciality it is. No training, no
  time
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-shot-covid-issue-171.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="GitHub issue: Your Wisconsin data looks horribly flawed"}

::: {.attribution}
[epiforecasts/covid#171](https://github.com/epiforecasts/covid/issues/171)
·
[Reflections on two years estimating effective reproduction numbers](https://samabbott.co.uk/posts/2022-03-25-rt-reflections/),
2022 · the rules from
[Data, Models, and Modellers during a Global Pandemic](https://samabbott.co.uk/posts/2023-01-04-iisa-data-models-and-modellers-during-a-global-pandemic/),
2023
:::
:::

## Collaborative forecasting hubs

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Each team submits weekly and the hub combines them into an ensemble
- The European hub ensemble beat 83% of teams' case forecasts and 91% of
  death forecasts on relative WIS, the weighted interval score

> However, they can be very hard to learn from, and though we have really
> tried to learn more about how to forecast it has been difficult.
>
> *Abbott, 2022*
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-hub-ensemble-good.png){height="640px"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="Relative WIS by country, ensemble marked as an asterisk"}

::: {.attribution}
Figure 4, [Sherratt et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.81916),
eLife, CC-BY 4.0 ·
[Evaluating an epidemiologically motivated surrogate model](https://samabbott.co.uk/posts/2022-10-13-surrogate-ensemble-forecast/),
2022
:::
:::
::::
